question: On 15 April 2026, the Commission declared the EU’s age verification app ‘technically ready’ for citizens and that it met ‘the highest privacy standards in the world.’ The app was positioned as a privacy-preserving, open-source tool to help enforce age limits on ‘online platforms’ under the Digital Services Act. Shortly after the launch, critics highlighted multiple concerns around rushed deployment, security and privacy failings, and threats posed to fundamental rights12345. Can the Commission clarify: 1.

whether all EU social media users will be required to undergo mandatory passport/ID age verification via this app before accessing platforms with an age limit, and, given the Commission’s repeated use of the term ‘online platforms’, does it wish to extend this obligation beyond social media platforms?
why it stated that the app was ‘technically ready’, given its technical vulnerabilities revealed by experts and concerns raised by researchers ahead of the announcement?
how it will protect the ability of at-risk citizens to maintain online anonymity if it obliges all EU citizens to link their accounts to government-issued IDs?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.7.2026) There is no specific mandatory method for age checks prescribed in the Digital Services Act1.

The guidelines on the protection of minors2 under the Digital Services Act set out clear guidance on the circumstances in which, depending on the level of risks, the Commission considers the use of age assurance methods, like age estimation or age verification, appropriate and proportionate measures to ensure a high level of privacy, safety, and security of minors.

The blueprint presented on 15 April 20263 is feature-complete and constitutes an early reference implementation of the European age verification solution. It was released openly for scrutiny prior to public deployment.

Some of the issues raised by independent experts were well founded and have been corrected by the development consortium, with an updated version made available shortly thereafter and further improvements to follow. The age verification blueprint does not require any linking of accounts to government-issued IDs.

The system has been specifically designed to enable users to prove their age without sharing any identity data or personal details. Platforms receive only a cryptographic confirmation (no raw data), which ensures unlinkability and no centralised storage of data is carried out. Although a government-issued ID may be used to generate the proof of age, this process relies exclusively on local device processing.
The ID is never transmitted to anyone, and any data used for the issuance is deleted once the issuance process has been performed.
